Definition: from G4692; "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness:--business, (earnest) care(-fulness), diligence, forwardness, haste.
BiblicalUsage: Diligence is eagerness with its sleeves up, and haste when it matters. Not slothful in business, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord; Jude gave all diligence to write of the common salvation; and Herodias's daughter came in straightway with haste to ask for John's head.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the same eagerness serves two masters, and the question is always what the haste is for.
